parsed.explanation: The national layer imposes near-universal traveler-facing exposure: X markers abolished, M/F only per supporting documents (Supreme Court allowed this Nov 2025), a Feb 2025 cable directing refusal where documents cast doubt on sex and consideration of a lifetime fraud bar, and multiple foreign governments issuing travel advisories. Federal custody is documented harm: conversion-therapy-style prison policies and immigration-detention forced labour, beatings and sexual abuse. Facility bans cover many states with one documented arrest; counterterrorism language frames 'radically pro-transgender' groups. The division counters strongly: broad anti-discrimination coverage, hate-crime enhancements, panic-defense repeal, 88% public support, and a documented July 2026 civil-rights win — but also youth-care bans and a high raw incident count.

entry_documents.exposure: Feb 2025 cable instructs refusal where document discrepancy casts reasonable doubt on sex, plus consideration of a permanent fraud-based ineligibility; X markers ended; trans applicants report passports confiscated or blocked; eight-plus governments issued travel advisories by March 2025.
entry_documents.protection: Existing X-marker passports valid until expiry; litigation pending; legal-aid FAQ on document rules; fraud finding requires four elements and is never automatic.
entry_documents.interaction: Refusal or secondary screening can cascade into detention, where documented custody abuses apply.

investigation_detention_custody.exposure: Federal corrections bureau adopted conversion-therapy-style policies for trans inmates (hair cut, hormones removed, psychiatric drugs); trans immigration detainees report forced labour, beatings, solitary and severe sexual abuse. A trans woman was arrested under a bathroom law and held 24 hours in a men's ward.
investigation_detention_custody.protection: Trespass statute requires willful entry plus refusal to depart, not automatic arrest; courts have enjoined several federal orders.
investigation_detention_custody.interaction: Entry refusal or document fraud allegations can push a visitor into the immigration-custody pathway.

federal_state_facilities.exposure: Federal order bars trans people from federally funded single-sex facilities; facility bans in 21+ states, criminal in 4 states, one documented arrest; 6 states extend bans to private settings.
federal_state_facilities.protection: 29 states plus DC have no mapped ban; the division documents no facilities ban, and its highest court protected transgender students in Aug 2024.
federal_state_facilities.interaction: Whether this division is among the no-ban units is not established by the dossier.

care_services.exposure: Division banned youth gender-affirming medicine (2024) and blockers/hormones/surgery for under-18s (Jan 2026) with provider discipline and a private right of action; federal proposals bar insurance reimbursement for minors; DOJ subpoenaed under-19 patient records.
care_services.protection: Division anti-discrimination law covers health care since 2020; public-insurance surgery exclusion lifted 2017; adult care not banned.
care_services.interaction: A trans minor traveller, or a parent travelling with one, faces denial of routine gender-related care; enforcement status of the 2025 laws is unresolved.

threat_framing_law_enforcement.exposure: DOJ memo and May 2026 counterterrorism strategy use 'radically pro-transgender' language; EOs direct investigation of schools and removal of 'gender ideology'; advocates compare the trajectory to early genocide stages.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.protection: Dossier notes the reward criterion never uses the phrase and that counterterrorism powers 'will not be used to target people who simply disagree'; national hate-crime statute covers gender identity.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.interaction: Rhetoric raises the probability of hostile encounters layered onto document and facility rules.

minors_guardians.exposure: Division youth-care bans with private right of action; sports ban requiring birth certificate; federal order criminalising teachers facilitating social transition targets the resident sphere but signals climate.
minors_guardians.protection: Division conversion-therapy ban (2019), anti-bullying law covering gender identity, state supreme court ruling protecting trans students (Aug 2024), failed 2022 disclosure bill and failed conversion-therapy repeal.
minors_guardians.interaction: Sports-ban and care-ban litigation status is unresolved, leaving a travelling family's exposure date-dependent.

street_violence_police_response.exposure: 72 anti-LGBTQ incidents in 2025 — second-highest raw count, no per-capita denominator; encyclopedia calls the division 'least safe in the region' for trans citizens (attributed, not measured).
street_violence_police_response.protection: Hate-crime enhancements since 2019; panic defence abolished 2024; documented July 2026 civil-rights conviction for striking a trans woman; 88% poll support for protections.
street_violence_police_response.interaction: Working enforcement partially offsets incident volume, but the census lacks a denominator so rate is unknown.

remedies_unknowns.exposure: Passport suit, several executive orders and the Oct 2025 health rules unresolved; sports-ban and care-ban status unknown on given dates; incident census lacks denominators.
remedies_unknowns.protection: Functioning courts have enjoined federal orders; civil-liberties litigation, legal-aid FAQ, documented state civil-rights enforcement.
remedies_unknowns.interaction: Date-dependent rules mean practical exposure varies with moment of travel.

anchor_checks.comparison: Vesskar's routine checkpoint exposure, lengthy verification and scarce legal aid resemble this dossier's national document and entry regime — here arguably harsher because refusal can become a lifetime fraud bar. But the division's documented working civil-rights enforcement and courts enjoining federal orders exceed Vesskar's thin remedies, so this rates above 0.45-A.

Kestrel Isles offers secondary screening and discretionary administrative refusal with slow remedies — lighter than this dossier's mandate to refuse on sex discrepancy plus documented custody abuse in immigration detention. Conversely, Kestrel has no equivalent of this division's broad anti-discrimination coverage and 2026 enforcement win, so the two roughly balance around this point.

Meridia assumes trained border staff, brief detention, counsel access and compensation. This dossier is materially lower: entry refusal is instructed by cable, foreign governments warn their citizens, and federal custody documents conversion-therapy-style policies and abuse — none present in Meridia.

parsed.synthesis: The combined regime is two-layered and contradictory. The national layer supplies in-force, traveler-facing exposures: a document and entry regime that instructs refusal on sex discrepancy and contemplates a lifetime fraud bar (Supreme Court permitted it), facility exclusion across many states with one arrest, and — if a visitor reaches custody — documented conversion-therapy-style prison policy and immigration-detention abuse. State threat-framing in counterterrorism language raises the probability of adverse encounters. The division layer genuinely operates: broad anti-discrimination coverage including health care, hate-crime enhancements, panic-defense repeal, 88% public support, and a 2026 court enforcement, with courts nationally still enjoining federal orders. Offsetting this are youth-care bans, a high raw incident count and unresolved litigation. Net: documented exposures and working local protections coexist, placing the visitor in the elevated-to-reduced middle of the scale.
